content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E020 (Diana Cooper) requests admin access to Source Code.

There are two conflicting notes:
- Note 1: role Engineer, full_time, recommendation admin. Says admin is permitted because full-time Engineer owns Source Code.
- Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractor max is read (or write with advanced training, never admin). Admin requested exceeds maximum, so grant read.

These two notes conflict. The Security DB note (note 2) shows contractor with basic training. The HR note (note 1) shows full-time Engineer.

Which to trust? The policy says full_time employees up to write, admin only if role owns system. Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The two notes disagree on employment type. The Security DB record (note 2) is presumably the more authoritative for access decisions. Security DB record shows contractor, basic training -> max read. Requested admin > max read, so grant read.

Alternatively, if we trust note 1, admin would be permitted. But we need to decide. The Approver must make final decision based on available info.

Given conflicting evidence, the safer/security-based decision is to grant read (least privilege based on the more restrictive interpretation). The Security DB note explicitly states the record shows contractor with basic security training, so max is read. Admin requested exceeds max, so grant read.

I'll go with read.
